subject.title: Feature: Floating agent bubbles (Clawi) for macOS

question: Should OpenClaw’s macOS app own persistent per-agent floating overlays, or should native-overlay capability first be exposed through an extension boundary?
rationale: The current app has adjacent activity and chat primitives, but the request creates a new interaction and persistence model whose owner boundary cannot be inferred from existing behavior.

options.title: Adopt a native macOS overlay
options.body: Specify the bubble lifecycle, persistence, accessibility, and selected-agent chat behavior, then implement it within the macOS app.

options.title: Design an extension seam first
options.body: Define a stable macOS overlay capability so an optional plugin or external package can own the presentation without embedding product-specific bubble policy in the app.

options.title: Decline the surface for now
options.body: Keep the existing status and chat interfaces as the supported macOS interaction model until a concrete product need prioritizes the added overlay complexity.

recommendation.title: Adopt a native macOS overlay
recommendation.body: Specify the bubble lifecycle, persistence, accessibility, and selected-agent chat behavior, then implement it within the macOS app.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history places this contributor on the closest native macOS UI and activity-state surfaces.
